subtitle: A battle suit moves through a world of unstable matter

body: Matterfall is Housemarque's PlayStation 4 side-scrolling shooter, first released in North America on 15 August 2017. Avalon Darrow fights through a futuristic world infected by alien Smart Matter, using an armoured suit to jump, dodge and fire at the surrounding threats. The player also creates platforms and protective structures, making the environment part of the available response. A dangerous space can therefore be altered as well as crossed. The game connects precise shooting to platform movement, asking the player to see where safety might be constructed while the next attack is already approaching.

Platform creation gives the player a way to turn the surrounding material into something useful, opening a position or approach that would otherwise be unavailable. Shields offer another intervention when ordinary movement does not provide enough protection. The player has to connect those capabilities with firing and dodging, recognising when to keep attacking and when the shape of the encounter should be changed first. The side-on presentation makes those relationships visible together. A platform is not merely a place supplied by the designer, but can become part of the player's immediate solution to a dangerous arrangement.

Tommi Hartikainen directed the project, with Jari Hokkanen designing. Announced at Paris Games Week in 2015, it reached PlayStation 4 in August 2017, with a soundtrack and console theme offered among its preorder extras. Critical responses were mixed, but the design continued Housemarque's interest in immediate action whose depth comes from combining a small number of abilities under pressure. Matterfall gives that approach a side-scrolling form, joining the demands of keeping a firing line clear to the physical problem of reaching a useful position while enemies and projectiles occupy the same space.
